messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: HIGH - streaming-decode-gpu-oom on cluster-infer-us-west1. 18/24 decode pods reporting OOMKill within last 6m. Estimated customer impact: request drops and 5xxs. Runbook: /runbooks/decode-oom

anna-oncall: ack, I'm on it. seeing lots of long sessions with `max_tokens=100000` from a single client id. GPU mem goes from 21GB -> 60GB in ~30s and then container restarts.

sam-sre: confirming metrics: NVML shows memory climb and persistent KV cache growth. top offending route: `/v1/stream` on model=redwood-lite-7b-quant.

ryan-ml: that model's KV caching isn't size-limited for streaming clients; large tokens + long prefix will blow up. we need to enforce a per-request token cap ASAP.

anna-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) enforce token cap at edge 2) route to quantized fallbacks with smaller KV footprint 3) kill offending sessions 4) scale up? scaling won't help if single request hogs memory.

ops-bot: Automated action: temporarily scaling down streaming concurrency to 50% on cluster-infer-us-west1 to reduce blast radius.

sam-sre: doing (1) now — patching gateway to clamp `max_tokens` to 4096 for streaming routes. applying traffic control rule:

```
# temp token clamp
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gateway-token-clamp
  namespace: infra
data:
  STREAM_MAX_TOKENS: "4096"
EOF
# then reload gateway
kubectl rollout restart deployment/gateway -n infra
```

anna-oncall: rolling the config. ETA for gateway to be back: ~90s.

maria-support: heads-up — I've already opened a ticket with the affected customer's CS rep (client: acme-ai, client-id: acme-9f2) and asked them to pause any bulk/synthetic traffic. awaiting confirmation.

jen-product: need a customer-facing status note if this is customer-caused; mark as potential misconfig. keep me in loop.

ryan-ml: also pushing a hotfix to the runtime to guard KV cache growth: add eviction threshold and per-session KV cap. patch draft:

```
// pseudo
if (session.kv_length > 20000) {
  evict_oldest_kv_entries(session, session.kv_length - 20000);
}
```

sam-sre: hotfix queued as canary to 2 pods in cluster-infer-us-west1-canary. deploying now.

ops-bot: canary redeploy complete on 2 pods. memory profile shows reduced KV growth on canary instances.

anna-oncall: gateway clamp is live. I'm observing incoming requests with `max_tokens` > 4096 being truncated at the gateway — drop rate on decode OOMs is down ~60% in the last 3m.

maria-support: acme-ai ops confirmed they had a CI job that accidentally set `max_tokens: 100000` for streaming tests. they've paused. asking for ETA on full fix.

sam-sre: plan: keep gateway clamp + KV eviction hotfix rolling to 30% over 30m, monitor OOMs. once stable, we will push to 100% and remove clamp if runtime guard is sufficient.

jen-product: if this is root caused by customer misconfig, include best-practice note in docs and send them a recommended default. also suggest API validation to prevent clients from setting absurd token caps.

ryan-ml: agreed — will open an RFC for server-side token validation and per-client quotas + adaptively sized KV caps.

anna-oncall: current status: 12/24 decode pods previously OOMing, now 3/24 after mitigations. request drops reduced from ~18% to ~2.4% for impacted routes. CPU and GPU utilization back to normal on canary.

ops-bot: incident-bot note: created incident ticket INC-2024-1783 and paged on-call rotation.

sam-sre: next immediate tasks: 1) continue roll to 30% and observe 2) identify and terminate any lingering sessions from acme-9f2 3) coordinate with infra to warm fallback pools (redwood-lite-quant-8b) for any ripples.

anna-oncall: terminating sessions for client acme-9f2 now: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/sessions/terminate -d '{"client_id":"acme-9f2"}'` — servers responded 200.

maria-support: CS to customer: short note drafted — "We saw an automated testing job set an excessively large max_tokens header which caused streaming sessions to exceed the node memory profile. We've applied a temporary clamp and applied guard rails; please do not resume the test until we confirm full remediation." Sending now.

ryan-ml: telemetry note: KV cache growth metric added to per-route dashboards and an alert to trigger at >50% of expected memory per session. will PR the dashboard.

sam-sre: rolling the KV eviction hotfix to 30% done. watching logs.

anna-oncall: update in last 5m: OOM counts per minute dropped from 12->1. memory usage stable. customer impact: majority of requests restored; a small subset (long sessions) still require manual kill if they were started prior to clamp.

jen-product: recommend we keep the clamp for the next 24h and follow up with a config/UI change to block `max_tokens` > 100k at API layer. also add a clearer error message when request is truncated.

maria-support: logging timeline and affected request ids to the incident ticket. will provide a post-incident customer impact summary after containment.

anna-oncall: final checklist before we close pager: 1) full rollout of KV eviction and runtime guard 2) gateway clamp extended + gradual relaxation plan 3) customer confirmation from acme-ai 4) postmortem assigned.

sam-sre: assigning postmortem to @sam-sre and @ryan-ml. I'll keep the incident open for 6 hours to verify stability, then we'll transition to ticket-only.

incident-bot: Incident update: Mitigated — severity decreased to MEDIUM. Ongoing monitoring window 6h. INC-2024-1783 updated.

maria-support: acme-ai confirmed they will update their test config and rerun after we give all-clear. offering a call with their engineering team if needed.

anna-oncall: thanks team — great quick coord. I'll file the blameless postmortem and include recommendations: API validation, per-client session caps, and clearer docs. closing the active pager.

sam-sre: thumbs up. follow-up actions tracked in INC-2024-1783.
